prompts.prompt: Edit the supplied ACTUAL UNITY GAMEPLAY SCREENSHOT into a deliberately modest, attainable visual planning mockup for AIRSIDE. This is the same indie Unity airport game with an entirely NEW UI design direction. HARD REQUIREMENT preserve screenshot airport layout, exact crossed runways, taxiways, flat satellite-based grass, apron and terminal location, suburban building masses, high overview camera, existing simple low-detail aircraft silhouettes and approximate current polygon budgets. Do not turn it into photograph, do not create a cinematic airport or realistic new aircraft, no ground-level camera, no new buildings, no fancy glass terminals, no terrain reconstruction. World should remain unmistakably this screenshot, with its modest simple game graphics. Only modest world polish: soften glaring white roof/apron into warm pale grey, shift near-black asphalt to charcoal grey while keeping markings, reduce noisy concrete/satellite contrast slightly, subdued dry-green grass, gentle existing game shadow contrast. Keep satellite texture visibly game-like. Remove ALL old UI: left rail, floating status boxes, first-flight guide, minimap, overlapping traffic labels. Replace with fresh 'AIRLINE DISPATCH DESK' design. Thin warm off-white header, ink text, left 'AIRSIDE / Soak Air', central text navigation 'Airport' active, 'Schedule', 'Network', 'Fleet', 'Career'; far right 'Adelaide 13:51' and small 'Menu'. Typography clean modern sans serif, squared corners, no glass transparency or neon. A slim TOP second line shows '$2,253  •  Reliability 100%  •  Provisional' unobtrusively, no big rounded panels. World occupies central 75 percent or more. At BOTTOM one horizontal warm off-white dispatch tray about 16 percent screen height, separated from world by fine line; heading 'YOUR NEXT FLIGHT' small, a single roomy row 'SA146' 'VH-PAX / Saab 340B' 'ADL → BHQ' 'Departs 14:01' 'Fuelling 10%' with a restrained blue short progress bar and one dark-blue button 'View rotation'. Far right text '1 aircraft' and 'All flights'. No redundant second inspector. One small blue selection marker at regional apron, no labels across airport. Show selected flight ID only near tray, other AI traffic only tiny optional markers. Add tiny caption bottom edge 'Attainable visual concept • based on existing gameplay'. This is a restrained believable UI-over-existing-engine mockup, NOT high-budget graphics. Main target is a fresh horizontal flight-first interface with current world preserved.

Using the supplied actual AIRSIDE Unity gameplay screenshot as the background and graphics ceiling, create a fresh practical 16:9 airline dispatch workspace UI concept. Preserve the current simple low-poly airport visible behind it, not photoreal. Completely replace the current left icon rail and giant dark modal. New design: narrow warm off-white horizontal top header 'AIRSIDE / Soak Air' and text destinations Airport, Schedule (active coastal-blue underline), Network, Fleet, Career, right 'Adelaide 13:50' and Menu. Clean humanist sans serif, dark ink, warm off-white opaque surfaces, thin rules, simple rectangular controls with small radius. Below header a centered large but spacious OFF-WHITE 'Schedule' workspace occupying middle 80 percent width and 65 percent height. LEFT two-thirds: a clear flight board table with column headers Flight, Aircraft, Route, Departure, State. One selected flight row: 'SA146 | VH-PAX | ADL → BHQ | 14:01 | Fuelling'. Below table airy empty space with quiet prompt 'Your next departure is in 11 minutes.' No fake extra owned fleet: current airline owns ONE aircraft. RIGHT one-third: a separated editing column titled 'Plan next rotation', rows Aircraft VH-PAX / Saab 340B, Destination Kingscote (KGC), Seats 25 / 34, Departure 14:06 with simple minus/plus controls. Transparent economics mock data from actual screenshot: 'Outbound −$337', 'Return about $396', 'Estimated profit +$188'. Clearly label values 'Illustrative'. One clear dark-blue primary button 'Schedule rotation', quieter 'Back to airport'. Bottom edge of workspace one small line 'Kingscote • regional route • 125 km'. Optional network context is a small correct simple line map of South Australia in lower LEFT empty area, modest not decorative with Adelaide and Kingscote southwest on Kangaroo Island; no geographic precision claim. Bottom page quiet persistent status '$2,253 • Reliability 100% • Provisional'. No aircraft photos, no complex charts, no giant dark cards, no competing alert boxes, no large display fonts. This should feel a new flight-first airline workstation while remaining feasible with Unity-rendered text, rows and vector shapes. Tiny lower caption 'Interface direction concept • existing simulation data'.

Edit supplied native Unity Saab 340 aircraft review sheet into an honest modest before/after art-plan comparison. HARD preserve actual aircraft mesh silhouette, SAME fuselage proportions and windows, current coarse geometry, actual low-mounted wing and simple engine nacelles, same low detail wheels, same Emu Air orange/white livery. Do not replace with a photographed aircraft or change to high-polygon detailed model. We are improving a small existing indie Unity game, not dreaming of flight simulator art. Produce a simple landscape two-column reference board on pale warm grey, title 'AIRSIDE / MODEST AIRCRAFT POLISH'. Left column heading 'Current native render' using the same provided side and front three-quarter views and current stark shading, unmodified aircraft shapes. Right column heading 'Proposed material pass' same two views, identical shape and same simple windows and doors, but reduced blown-white glare, slightly warmer off-white painted body, gentler grey shading, subtle non-shiny engine metal, dark grey tyres, less harsh cockpit glass and consistent modest muted ochre paint. Keep aircraft simple and low-poly; exactly same detail level as left, no extra rivets or seams or added gear parts. If adding fine panel accents keep them very restrained, no photographic dirt. Add ground contact shadow under ONLY proposed row for visual grounding but do not alter gear. Under both columns short clean labels 'Same mesh' 'Calmer paint' 'Clearer shading'. Bottom a small honest strip 'First pass: materials and lighting. Later: reference-check silhouette, doors and landing gear.' All text clear, no claims performance verified, no AAA lighting. This board is an approximate visual hypothesis, not a measured before/after engine test. Tiny footer 'Concept edit of native render — proposed result unverified'.
